 Almaty R2 previews and predictions: Khachanov vs. Machac, Bublik vs. Marozsan 
 October 21, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 22 
 In a stacked section of the draw, Karen Khachanov goes up against Tomas Machac during second-round action in Almaty on Thursday. The winner will face either Alexander Bublik or Fabian Marozsan in the quarterfinals. 
 Tomas Machac vs. (5) Karen Khachanov
Khachanov and Machac will be going head-to-head for the second time in their careers when they clash in round two of the Almaty Open on Thursday. Their only previous meeting came at the 2024 Australian Open, where Khachanov prevailed 6-4, 7-6(4), 4-6. 7-6(5). Based on respective current form, 25th-ranked Russian should be in good shape to prevail again. He made a run to the U.S. Open semifinals and is 10-3 in his last 13 matches following a 6-2, 6-4 rout of Rei Sakamoto on Tuesday.
Machac is coming down the stretch of an injury-plagued 2026 campaign. The 26-year-old Czech is struggling down at No. 72 in the world with a 16-15 record this season. Machac easily beat unknown Kazakh wild card Zangar Nulanuly on Wednesday, but he doesn’t have a single top-50 victory since Roland Garros and has not defeated anyone ranked as high as Khachanov since Monte-Carlo. 
 Pick: Khachanov in 2

 (3) Alexander Bublik vs. Fabian Marozsan
Bublik is not a Nitto ATP Finals contender (in part because he skipped Masters 1000 events in Montreal and Cincinnati), but he has — when interested — put together another fine season. The 19th-ranked Kazkah has once again been effective on all three surfaces, beginning the year with a title in Hong Kong (hard), finishing runner-up in Kitzbuhel (clay), and reaching the Stuttgart semis and the Wimbledon fourth round (grass). 
Whereas Bublik earned a first-round bye as Almaty’s No. 3 seed, Marozsan advanced with a 7-5, 7-6(4) over another Kazakh — Timofey Skatov — on Tuesday. However, the 64th-ranked Hungarian has won back-to-back matches at an ATP tournament just three times since March. Bublik should be at least somewhat motivated in front of the home crowd this week, so look for him to take care of an opponent who is not especially skilled on indoor hard courts.
 Pick: Bublik in 2
